intro.title: Build offline first notes with localStorage fallback
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple notes application that saves your data locally in the browser, ensuring it works even without an internet connection. You'll learn how to use the localStorage API to store, retrieve, and update data persistently. The core programming concepts involve handling JavaScript objects, managing application state, and implementing fallback logic for offline scenarios. By the end, you'll have a functional app that demonstrates offline-first principles using fundamental web technologies like HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
intro.usecase: Offline-first patterns with localStorage fallback are essential in modern web applications that need to function reliably despite network issues. For example, note-taking apps like Google Keep or Notion use this approach to let users create and edit notes seamlessly, syncing data to the cloud only when connectivity is restored. Similarly, form-heavy applications such as survey tools or e-commerce checkouts implement this to prevent data loss if a user's connection drops mid-entry. This pattern ensures a smooth, uninterrupted user experience, making it a practical skill for building resilient, user-centric software.
